name: 09-field-notes
prompt: Use case: logo-brand. Create ONE original Chinese typographic logo for the crop observation project named exactly "禾观". Render these two simplified Chinese characters correctly, clearly and legibly: 禾观. This is a warm thoughtful personal agricultural technology project, not a big corporate agriculture company. The user rejected all earlier generic leaf, sprout, eye, field, book and cartoon symbols as ugly, meaningless, too generic or too commercial. Start fresh with the Chinese name itself as the identity. Do not add an icon next to the text. Do not paste leaves or magnifiers onto normal typography. The character forms themselves must carry the design. Aim for convincing bespoke lettering with expert optical spacing and distinctive character, moderate visual richness, a logo someone could remember. Finished professional graphic design, not default font samples, not an illustration. Flat ink on a plain warm ivory background, no shadows, no gradients, no texture, no mockup. No explanatory text, no captions, no extra Chinese text, no slogans. Only the wordmark 禾观 and a small carefully spaced secondary Latin line "AGRISCAN" below. Large centered artwork with generous empty margin. Direction: a beautiful FIELD NOTEBOOK signature, humble and quietly intelligent. Draw 禾观 in bespoke semi-handwritten Chinese lettering, substantial dark moss-green ink, medium-wide strokes with gentle variation, slightly uneven human rhythm but controlled modern forms, highly legible, neither cursive calligraphy nor childish handwriting. Let the main descending stroke of 禾 suggest a rooted crop through its taper and natural branching structure WITHOUT drawing a literal plant. Let 观 have an open airy interior as a deliberate gesture of attentive looking. Both characters stand firmly on a shared baseline and have an intimate balanced relationship. Add one short muted clay-red stroke underneath the central gap as a subtle observation underline, integrated and discreet. Small AGRISCAN beneath in a modest widely spaced humanist sans serif. The result feels like a botanist's authored field journal title, literary, lively and credible. Landscape 3:2 composition.
